samples.summary: Undo floor now fails OPEN: the boundary that stops a user undoing past the initial document load is enforced by object identity against a test-only SDK accessor, and "marker not found" is interpreted as "everything is undoable".
samples.evidence: `canUndo()` was `stack.length > undoFloor` (fail-closed by construction: an unknown/odd stack shape could only refuse undos). It is now `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2977), where `undoFloorMark` is one entry captured by reference from `doc.getUndoStackForTest()` (line 859). The comment states the intended fail-open case (cap dropped the floor). But the same `-1` answer is returned for ANY reason the marker is not found by reference — e.g. if the SDK's `getUndoStackForTest()` ever returns copied/cloned entries (it is an undocumented `...ForTest` accessor with no stability contract, and this repo pins `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.19 without a compile-time guarantee about identity), or if the SDK rebuilds entries on a remote-change/GC pass. In that case the floor silently disappears on every call and the protection `setDocument()` explicitly documents — "Users must not be able to undo past it — doing so would destroy blocks the cursor still references" (yorkie-doc-store.ts:~616) — is gone for all users, in a shared CRDT document, with no visible symptom until content is destroyed. I could not confirm or refute the SDK's identity semantics: node_modules is not present in this checkout (`node_modules/*` glob empty), so I traced only the call sites in-repo. A fail-closed formulation (e.g. keep a monotonically increasing write counter, or verify the marker was present at least once and treat a lost marker as "floor at index 0") would degrade safely. Note also that the three sibling stores (yorkie-note-store.ts:353, yorkie-slides-store.ts:654, yorkie-board-store.ts:514) still use the depth form, so the two designs now disagree about the same boundary.

samples.summary: The clipboard-read continuation re-validates `disposed` and `pasting` after the await but not the view-only (`readOnly`) gate that authorized the write; correct only because `readOnly` happens to be immutable today.
samples.evidence: `pastePlainTextFromClipboard()` is authorized solely by the `if (this.readOnly) { ... return; }` gate in `handleKeyDown` (text-editor.ts:1096-1112), then awaits `navigator.clipboard.readText()` (line 4245) — a wait that can span a permission prompt, i.e. arbitrarily long user interaction. The change adds `if (this.disposed || this.pasting) return;` (line 4254) but does not re-read `this.readOnly`, so the permission decision made before the yield is never re-checked at the write. Today this is not exploitable: `readOnly` is assigned once in the constructor (text-editor.ts:719) with no setter, and under `readOnly` the editor additionally runs over `readOnlyDocStore()` (store/read-only.ts:67), whose proxy neuters every mutator and whose `batch(fn)` only runs the body while the writes inside remain no-ops — so even an unauthorized continuation would write nothing. The finding is that this async write path is now the one place where an authorization decision is separated from its write by an unbounded wait, and the file itself notes the server-side check behind the flag ships in shadow mode by default (store/read-only.ts:38-42), making the client flag the real write boundary. Re-checking `this.readOnly` alongside `disposed`/`pasting` costs one condition and makes the path robust if read-only ever becomes a runtime state (e.g. permission revoked mid-session).

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as quoted: `undoFloorMark` is captured by identity from `doc.getUndoStackForTest()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:858-861) and `canUndo()` returns `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1` (:2977), which is fail-open when the marker is not found. However this is not a security defect under the Security lens. (1) The undo floor is not an authorization boundary: it constrains the same already-authorized editor who is writing the document, and its only consumer is the editor's own UI path (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2317). That editor can destroy the same content with ordinary permitted writes, so no privilege boundary, IDOR, or role check is involved. (2) The actual access-control boundary for this store is the read-only proxy in packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:21-30, where `canUndo` is merely an allowlisted reader and `undo()` is absent and therefore neutered to a no-op (read-only.ts:59-65, with getPrototypeOf/set/defineProperty/deleteProperty traps at 50-58); a `true` from canUndo cannot help a viewer because the mutator behind it is already stubbed. So this change cannot weaken any permission gate. (3) What remains is a robustness/data-integrity concern contingent on a hypothetical future change in an undocumented SDK accessor's identity semantics — the correctness and blast-radius lenses, explicitly deferred here. No secret, injection sink, signature/HMAC check, weak randomness, SSRF, deserialization, or path-traversal vector is implicated.
